cR.role: candidate cold: the rank-cut producer's cold path, which is the stacked producer's code (KIC_RANK_SOLVE is read only by the rank stage, which a cold process skips); its own processes, so the candidate's end-to-end cost is measured on its own rows

cRI.role: secondary (optional component): cR with lift_scan canonicalizing the index build (KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift; the stacked run's cSI, 1.33x cold without rank)

cS.role: baseline cold: the stacked producer (koblitz-n83-stacked-20261016 arm cS, the n=83 baseline of docs/ic/BASELINES.md), setup + one-target online with the verified cached factor-log table

kR.role: candidate rank stage: kS with the partner roots by point addition from each stored root's y (KIC_RANK_SOLVE=padd), exact S3 order resolved at every hit, then one target

kRX.role: planted positive control: kR plus the work it removes (the S3 batch solve and both partners' normal-basis maps on every candidate), redone, compared with the point-addition pair as a set on every input and discarded

kRaa.role: A/A control: a second process of kR

kS.role: baseline rank stage: the stack's (lift_scan, Feistel, the 16-byte compact loop over the folded index, partner roots by the batched S3 root solve), then one target

rT.role: A's tuned rho rT770 (Fold/64/DP6), the strongest one-target rho at n=83, same points

controls_pass_rule.planted: rank stage kRX / kR (per-attempt cost, attempts paired within blocks), 95% bootstrap lower bound above 1

design.process_model: one point per process, fresh process per run, one pinned CPU, one runner
design.rank_seeds_note: 201.. are new (the stacked run used 101 and 102); each seed fixes 600 new rank targets [a]G - R_j
design.runtime_estimate: from run 38862448935: build and tests about 15 min; cold segment about 90 s (cS, cR about 26 s each, cRI about 20 s, rT 3 s); rank block about 1,050 s (kS about 282 s, kR and kRaa about 220 s if the local per-probe ratio holds, kRX about 300 s); 4 blocks; total about 2.3 h, up to about 3 h on a slower runner

exactness_argument: For points R, T of E(F_2^83) with x(R) != x(T), the two roots of S3(x(R), x(T), X) are x(T + R) and x(T - R), so the point-addition pair equals the S3 loop's pair as a set. Every stored root is the x of a point of E (it is x(P1 +- P2)); its y is recovered by the half-trace, and the Frobenius conjugates (x^(2^s), y^(2^s)) are points of E because E is defined over F_2. The keys are the same canonical rotations of the same normal-basis values; only the order inside a pair could differ, and at every root-table hit the S3 pair is recomputed with the S3 solver, asserted equal to the emitted pair as a set, and the pair is evaluated in the S3 order at the S3 loop's probe positions. Inputs exceptional for the S3 batch (zero denominator) are solved by the S3 solver itself. So the first hit, the lift, the relation and the probe count of every attempt are the S3 loop's; the attempts are a function of the rank seed and the earlier relations, so the echelon and the factor-log table are the baseline's. Tested on a 9-orbit base (every loop, both orders, a deliberately swapped emission order) and checked on every input of every kRX rank stage.
gates: every scheduled row valid (exit 0, verified, schedule match, no memory event)

every IC process: lift_scan, Feistel, prefetch; the 16-byte compact table with 2^26 slots over the folded index (14,940,300 stored of 29,880,000 logical states); 29,878,182 table entries; logical-state blake3 and table-map digests equal B's (online.index_digest); no root bloom
per point: one scalar across every IC process (cold and rank) and rT, replayed as [d]G = Q in the pinned oracle
per point: one relation (point indices) and one probe count across every IC process on the point
Q0 (O1): cS and cR give the archived Feistel relation and scalar with 1,987,852 probes
rank arms: full rank, the arm's KIC_RANK_SOLVE recorded, and the written factor-log table equal to B's archived table, log for log

per rank block: rank_relations_blake3, the per-attempt probe vector (600 entries) and rank_root_calls_total identical across kS, kR, kRaa and kRX (the candidate keeps every relation and every probe of the baseline, not only the table)
kRX: rank_padd_plant_checked_inputs > 0 (every input of its rank stage compared with the S3 roots)
multiplicity: one primary statistic; every secondary is descriptive and never changes the verdict

online.cold_interval: producer's own clock: process start (main) .. recovery_check_end of the one target = setup_complete + the five online phases (cold_in_process_ms); in ic_cold the rank stage is skipped (verified cached table); the index digest runs after the target, outside every interval

question: Does computing the rank stage's partner roots by point addition (x(T+R), x(T-R) from the stored root's recovered y and one batched inversion per candidate, instead of the batched S3 root solve), with the S3 order resolved exactly at every root-table hit, lower the END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) of the stacked n=83 K600 producer on new targets and new rank seeds, with every rank relation, every per-attempt probe count, every scalar and the factor-log table unchanged?

statistics.primary: R = E2E(kS, cS) / E2E(kR, cR). Bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261016: the rank blocks resampled with replacement; within each drawn block the attempt indices resampled with replacement and used for both kS and kR (the gate makes attempt i the same target with the same probes in both), each process's non-attempt time kept; the cold points resampled, paired across cS and cR

the point-addition counters per rank process (fallback states, irregular inputs, resolved hits, swapped pairs)
